device.category: semi-modular analogue percussion synthesizer with 8-step sequencer, MIDI/USB and 16-voice poly chain, desktop or Eurorack
device.based_on: Recreation of the Moog DFAM (2017, modelled separately), which the guide does not name; same voice, sequencer and patchbay, with pink noise, MIDI/USB clock and poly chain added. Guide V1.0, November 2021.

sources.title: Behringer EDGE Quick Start Guide V1.0 (2021)
sources.note: Multilingual; English used. Hook-up diagrams (including poly chain), numbered controls 1-63, getting started, three patch ideas, default patch drawing, SynthTribe note and specifications.

sources.title: Behringer, EDGE product page
sources.note: 'MIDI plays the sounds, and MIDI, USB or an external clock can drive the sequencer'; 'dual 8-step sequencer' meaning the pitch and velocity rows.

sources.title: ModWiggler, 'Behringer EDGE' thread (owner reports)
sources.note: MIDI notes play the voice; VELOCITY OUT follows MIDI note velocity as well as the velocity row; holding ADVANCE lets each MIDI note step the sequencer, with PITCH OUT following the pitch row; one owner hears less low-end roundness than the DFAM.

sources.title: Sweetwater, 'Getting Started with Behringer SYNTHTRIBE'
sources.note: Generic SynthTribe settings across Behringer synths: MIDI channel (overrides DIP switches), pitch bend, key priority, MIDI transpose, multi trigger; Poly Chain tab with device count, voice mode and Enable.

sources.title: B&H Photo, Behringer EDGE listing
sources.note: Describes a '15x10 I/O matrix' and '44 real-time controls'.

architecture.polyphony_mode: monophonic percussion voice; up to 16 voices by chaining units over MIDI THRU (poly chain)
architecture.patch_memory_note: No memory; the sequencer is analogue (knob per step). MIDI channel set by rear DIP switches or SynthTribe.
architecture.summary: Two VCOs (10-octave range, triangle or square) with hard sync and VCO 1 -> VCO 2 linear FM; a pitch envelope shared by both VCOs at separate bipolar depths. VCO 1, VCO 2 and noise (or EXT AUDIO) are mixed into a 4-pole ladder filter, low- or high-pass, 20 Hz to 20 kHz, moved by its own envelope and by noise (or the VCF MOD input). The VCA envelope (1 ms or 100 ms attack) shapes the output. Every envelope is a decay with voltage-controlled time, its peak set by the step's VELOCITY. The 8-step sequencer has PITCH (±5 V) and VELOCITY (0-5 V) per step and a voltage-controlled clock VCO (10 to 10,000 BPM). The EDGE adds pink noise, MIDI or USB clock with a SCALE division, MIDI in and out/thru, USB MIDI and poly chaining.

modules.name: Sequencer clock VCO
modules.description: Clock oscillator, 0.7 Hz to 700 Hz (about 10 to 10,000 BPM at 16ths); 1 V/oct TEMPO input reaches audio rate. CLOCK switch selects INT/EXT, MIDI or USB; MIDI/USB clock is divided by SCALE (10-300 BPM).

modules.name: 8-step sequencer
modules.description: Analogue 8-step sequencer: PITCH (±5 V, about 10 octaves) and VELOCITY (0-5 V) per step, step LEDs, RUN/STOP, ADVANCE, TRIGGER.

modules.name: Trigger bus
modules.description: Sequencer triggers (normalled to the TRIGGER input) fire all three envelopes and the TRIGGER output (about 1 ms, +5 V).

modules.name: Velocity bus
modules.description: Step velocity (normalled to the VELOCITY input) sets the peak, and slightly lengthens the decay, of all three envelopes.

modules.name: OSC EG
modules.description: Attack 1 ms; decay set by its knob plus a ±5 V CV; peak and decay scaled by velocity. Output 0 to +8 V.

modules.name: VCF EG
modules.description: Attack 1 ms; decay set by its knob plus a ±5 V CV; peak and decay scaled by velocity. Output 0 to +8 V.

modules.name: VCA EG
modules.description: Attack 1 ms or 100 ms (VCA EG switch); decay set by its knob plus a ±5 V CV; peak and decay scaled by velocity. Output 0 to +8 V.

modules.name: OSC 1
modules.description: Analogue VCO, 10-octave range, triangle or square.

modules.name: OSC 2
modules.description: Analogue VCO, 10-octave range, triangle or square. Hard sync to VCO 1 and linear FM from VCO 1.

modules.name: Noise generator
modules.description: White noise, or pink with the NOISE COLOR switch; mixer source (unless EXT AUDIO is patched) and the default VCF modulation source.

modules.name: Mixer
modules.description: VCO 1, noise/external and VCO 2 levels into the filter; high levels clip pleasantly. The noise/ext channel has a CV-controlled level (NOISE LEVEL input).

modules.name: VCF modulation
modules.description: Scales noise (or the VCF MOD input, which replaces it) into the cutoff; the only direct CV path to the cutoff.

modules.name: VCF (ladder)
modules.description: 4-pole (-24 dB/octave) ladder filter, low-pass or high-pass, 20 Hz to 20 kHz; self-oscillates above about 3:00 resonance in LP (in HP only near 1 kHz).

properties.self_oscillates: LP above 3:00 resonance; HP only around 1 kHz

modules.name: VCA
modules.description: Output VCA driven by the VCA EG, summed with the VCA CV input.

modules.name: Output
modules.description: VOLUME to the VCA patch output (Eurorack level) and a 3.5 mm stereo phones jack.

modules.name: MIDI / USB
modules.panel_section: rear [MIDI IN, OUT/THRU, USB, MIDI CHANNEL]
modules.description: MIDI DIN in, DIN out or thru, and class-compliant USB MIDI: clock (with SCALE), note input, poly chaining.

connections.note: ADV/CLOCK replaces the clock VCO; TEMPO is ignored.
MIDI notes play the voice (Behringer; ModWiggler owners); which VCOs follow is not stated.
Notes fire the envelopes; with ADVANCE held they also step the sequencer (ModWiggler).
VELOCITY OUT follows MIDI note velocity as well as the velocity row (ModWiggler owner report).

indicators.label: POWER LED
indicators.function: On with power; red when poly mode is active.

behaviours.name: Signal path
behaviours.rule: VCO 1, noise/ext and VCO 2 are mixed into the LP/HP ladder filter, then the VCA (VCA EG), then VOLUME.

behaviours.name: Velocity and envelopes
behaviours.rule: Each step's VELOCITY sets the peak of all three decay envelopes (and slightly lengthens their decay), so it shapes loudness, punch and accent; zero velocity is silent.

behaviours.name: Pitch envelope
behaviours.rule: One pitch envelope reaches both VCOs at separate bipolar depths; positive for spikes (kicks), negative for dips. With both depths centred its decay does nothing. Typical decay 9-10:00 for drum punch.

behaviours.name: Sequencer pitch
behaviours.rule: SEQ PITCH MOD sends the PITCH knobs to both VCOs, VCO 2 only, or neither (PITCH output only, e.g. to VCA DECAY for hi-hat variation).

behaviours.name: Oscillator interaction
behaviours.rule: HARD SYNC locks VCO 2 to VCO 1 (VCO 2 below VCO 1 may be near silent, especially square). 1→2 FM is linear, clearest with sync off.

behaviours.name: Noise roles
behaviours.rule: Noise is a sound source (snares, hats, attack) and the default cutoff modulator (dirt, sizzle). EXT AUDIO replaces it in the mixer; VCF MOD replaces it as modulator.

behaviours.name: Filter
behaviours.rule: LP or HP, 20 Hz to 20 kHz; EG amount raises or lowers cutoff in either mode. Self-oscillation above about 3:00 resonance in LP; in HP only near 1 kHz.

behaviours.name: VCA attack
behaviours.rule: FAST: 1 ms (as the other envelopes). SLOW: 100 ms, softer attacks and a glide-like effect on bass lines.

behaviours.name: Clock and sync
behaviours.rule: The clock is a VCO (TEMPO CV is 1 V/oct, to audio rate). ADV/CLOCK steps the sequencer per rising edge and overrides TEMPO; RUN/STOP input runs while high. Sync units by TRIGGER OUT into ADV/CLOCK (start the follower first).

behaviours.name: Stopped-sequencer editing
behaviours.rule: With the sequencer stopped, ADVANCE steps without sounding and TRIGGER replays the current step.

behaviours.name: Pitch safety
behaviours.rule: Several pitch sources sum, so VCOs can leave the audible range; recover by centring FREQ, then EG amounts, then SEQ PITCH MOD off.

behaviours.name: MIDI and USB clock
behaviours.rule: CLOCK selects INT/EXT (TEMPO or ADV/CLOCK), MIDI or USB; with external clock SCALE sets step length (1/4 to 1/32, straight or triplet) and the tempo range is 10-300 BPM.

behaviours.name: Poly chain
behaviours.rule: Up to 16 units chained by MIDI THRU act as a 16-voice instrument; the power LED turns red in poly mode. Generic SynthTribe procedure: set all units to one channel, chain THRU to IN, choose the unit count and voice mode in the Poly Chain tab, press Enable.

behaviours.name: Playing from MIDI
behaviours.rule: MIDI notes play the voice. Owners report the sequencer section then idles, but holding ADVANCE makes each note step the sequencer, so the PITCH row (via PITCH OUT) can modulate per note; VELOCITY OUT then follows note velocity rather than the velocity row.

behaviours.name: Noise colour
behaviours.rule: White noise is bright; pink is darker.

behaviours.name: Warm-up
behaviours.rule: Allow 15 minutes (longer from cold) for tuning to settle.

Research filled: MIDI notes play the voice and carry velocity; ADVANCE-hold stepping; generic SynthTribe poly chain procedure and settings; see sources.
source_inconsistencies: EG (VCO 1&2) DECAY is described as modulating the pitch of both oscillators and increasing 'the amount of modulation', i.e. as a depth rather than a decay time (control 6).
The title promises a 'Dual 8-Step Sequencer'; there is one 8-step sequencer with pitch and velocity rows.
Getting Started calls the waveforms 'pulse or triangle'; the controls list and specifications say square or triangle.
Getting Started refers to an 'OSC 1&2 CV input'; the patchbay has separate OSC 1 CV and OSC 2 CV jacks.
Getting Started says NOISE/VCF MOD 'will add noise if no audio is present in the EXT AUDIO input', conflating the mixer's EXT AUDIO with the VCF MOD input.
The OSC EG output is labelled 'OSG EG' (control 52); 'OCILLATOR' heading typo.
Control numbers 23-25 are printed out of order against their descriptions, so ENVELOPE (FILTER), NOISE/VCF MOD and TEMPO cannot be matched to numbers with certainty.
Between sources: B&H describes a '15x10 I/O matrix'; the guide's patchbay has 15 inputs and 9 outputs plus PHONES.

modelling_gaps.detail: The guide gives only an outline; note pitch, gate and velocity paths come from owner reports and are marked inferred where unconfirmed. Poly chain and key priority settings follow Behringer's generic SynthTribe guidance.
Built on the same module graph as the DFAM file; differences are additions (noise colour, clock source, SCALE, MIDI/USB, phones, power switch).
